paragraphs: Rabbi Yehudah bar Gamda of Kefar Akko. (A tanna.) He is mentioned in [Sotah 43b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.43b.12): ‘Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel permits [it] in the name of Rabbi Yehudah bar Gamda of Kefar Akko.’ The saying appears in Tosefta, Kilayim, chapter 1, in the name of Rabbi Yehudah ben Agra. In the [Mekhilta, Yitro, Massekhta de-Amalek, chapter 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Mekhilta_DeRabbi_Yishmael,_Tractate_Amalek.4.3), Yehudah of Kefar Akko asked Rabban Gamliel.[^1]
We also find Rabbi Shimon ben Yehudah of Kefar Akko, a student of Rabbi Shimon, in [Sotah 37b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sotah.37b.5-6); see his entry.

notes.text: The Sotah ruling concerns layering a tree into a vegetable plant. Tosefta names Yehudah ben Agra rather than Gamda. The Mekhilta passage is numbered Amalek 4:3 in the linked edition, corresponding to the second section on Yitro.
